questions.q: What was the actual root cause found in WKSTN-FIN-14's forensic triage capture?
options: A disguised scheduled task, created minutes after the foreign sign-in, that relaunched a remote-access tool on every startup
A missing Windows security patch
A weak local administrator password
A corrupted system file unrelated to the incident
questions.explain: The scheduled task MicrosoftEdgeUpdateTaskMachineUA was named to blend in with real Windows update tasks but was the attacker's persistence mechanism.

questions.q: Why did the team restore WKSTN-FIN-14 from a verified-clean backup instead of just deleting the malicious scheduled task on the live machine?
options: SYSTEM-level persistence meant the attacker may have planted something else the triage capture didn't catch, so rebuilding was the safer eradication
Deleting scheduled tasks is technically impossible on a running machine
Backups are always required by company policy regardless of severity
It was faster than removing the single task
questions.explain: Trusting a host with attacker-level persistence on it is risky; a verified-clean backup removes that uncertainty entirely.

questions.q: What three things did validation check before WKSTN-FIN-14 returned to production?
options: A clean Defender for Endpoint scan, a scheduled task list matching baseline, and a tenant-wide re-run of the forensic query for the same indicators
Only that the user could log back in successfully
Only that the backup file existed
Only that the account password had been changed
questions.explain: Validation confirmed the host itself was clean and that the same indicators didn't exist anywhere else in the tenant.

questions.q: What had to happen before Teresa Marsh's account was re-enabled?
options: A forced password reset and MFA re-registration
Nothing — the account was re-enabled immediately once the host was restored
A new analytics rule had to be written first
Her manager had to personally approve the technical remediation steps
questions.explain: The account was re-enabled only after a forced password reset and MFA re-registration, closing off the stolen credential entirely.

questions.q: What makes the after-action report in this lesson different from a narrative retelling of the incident?
options: Each finding is paired with a concrete, owned, and dated follow-up item
It omits any technical detail about what happened
It is written only for executives and contains no action items
It replaces the need for a lessons-learned meeting entirely
questions.explain: Each of the four findings lists a specific follow-up action, an owning team, and a due date — not just a summary of events.
